🧠 How the System Works
Scoring Engine → Decision Zones → Decision States → Star Rating → BUY / WATCH / SHORT / AVOID
🎯  Scoring Engine — 5 Pillars, 100 Points
📊 Technicals — max 35 pts
EMA Stack (8/13/20/50/200)10 ptsFull bull stack (8>13>20>50) = 10; partial = 5; bearish = 0
RSI (Wilder 14)5 pts50-70 = bullish momentum; >70 overbought penalty; <30 oversold
MACD (12/26/9)4 ptsSignal line cross + histogram direction
Squeeze (BBands in KC)4 ptsSqueeze firing on direction = 4; squeeze on = 2
Volume (RVOL + OBV)4 ptsRVOL >=2x + OBV rising = 4; >=1.5x = 2
S/R Structure4 ptsWithin 1.25 ATR of support + >3% from resistance = 4
Chart Patterns (VCP etc.)4 ptsPocket pivot, 52wk breakout, bull flag, VCP = up to 4
🔥 Catalyst Quality — max 20 pts
PEAD (post-earnings drift)6 ptsTier 1: <21d post-earnings, EPS beat >5%, positive drift
UOA (unusual options activity)5 ptsTier 1: Large OTM sweep = institutional positioning
VCP Breakout4 ptsTier 1: 2+ contracting bases, declining volume, near pivot
Pocket Pivot3 ptsTier 2: Volume > max down-day volume in 10 bars
Squeeze / Momentum2 ptsTier 2-3: TTM squeeze, continuation signals
🌟 RS + Sector — max 20 pts
RS Rank vs SPY (63d)12 pts>=90 = 12, >=80 = 10, >=70 = 8, >=60 = 5, <50 = 0
Sector Rotation8 ptsSector ETF outperforming SPY over 20d = 8; underperform = 0
💼 Smart Money — max 15 pts
Order Blocks4 ptsInstitutional supply/demand zones — price reacting at OB = 4
Fair Value Gaps (FVGs)3 ptsUnfilled imbalance zones acting as magnets
Liquidity Sweeps3 ptsStop hunt below lows followed by reversal = 3
BOS / CHoCH3 ptsBreak of structure / change of character — trend shift signals
Insider Activity2 ptsNet open-market buys = 2; congressional alignment = +1
🎯 Quality Gate (Fundamentals) — max 10 pts
Revenue Growth (YoY)3 pts>20% = 3, 10-20% = 2, 0-10% = 1, negative = 0
Margin Quality3 ptsOperating margin trend + gross margin vs sector median
EPS Growth + Beat Rate2 pts>25% EPS growth = 2; beat rate >=75% = +1 bonus
Balance Sheet2 ptsCurrent ratio >=1.5, D/E <100% = 2
💡 Pullback Bonus: Stocks near a rising 50 SMA get penalty cancellation + RS bonus. This rewards healthy pullbacks in strong uptrends.

⭐  Star Rating (1-5)
Each stock receives a 1-5 star rating based on five weighted components. Stars provide a quick visual summary of overall trade quality.
R:R Ratio1.5 pts max>=5:1 = 1.5, >=4:1 = 1.2, >=3:1 = 0.9, >=2:1 = 0.5, <2:1 = 0
RS Rank1.0 pt max>=90 = 1.0, >=80 = 0.8, >=70 = 0.6, >=60 = 0.3, <60 = 0
Setup Quality1.0 pt maxBased on pillar score: >=85 = 1.0, >=75 = 0.7, >=65 = 0.4
Catalyst Tier0.5 pt maxCat T1 = 0.5, Cat T2 = 0.3, Cat T3 = 0.1

🏭 Hedge Fund Trading Framework
The principles that separate a trading system from a stock screener. Every BUY signal must answer these questions before capital is committed.
⚠️ The Core Problem: This Is a Screener, Not Yet a Trading System
A screener finds candidates. A trading system answers 5 questions before every trade:
  1. WHY does this stock move in the next 2–5 days specifically?
  2. WHO is on the other side — and why are they wrong?
  3. HOW MUCH do I risk given regime, volatility, and conviction?
  4. EXACTLY WHEN do I exit — win or lose?
  5. WHAT PATTERN OF LOSSES tells me the system stopped working?
The system currently answers none of these. It outputs BUY. A hedge fund trader cannot trade a BUY signal — they need a thesis.
⚖ The Timeframe Mismatch — Why Fundamentals Are Wrong for Swing Trading
The 4-pillar model mixes three completely different investment timeframes. A company's ROE does not change in 5 days. Its price does.
❌ Current (Wrong for 5-day swings)
Fundamentals 30 pts → 6–18 month relevant
Technicals 30 pts → correct timeframe ✓
Optionality 20 pts → correct timeframe ✓
Sentiment 10 pts → correct timeframe ✓
✅ Target (Swing-optimized weights)
Technicals 40 pts → trend, momentum, pattern, volume
Catalyst 25 pts → WHY this stock moves NOW
Smart Money 20 pts → who's accumulating before the move
Quality Gate 15 pts → solvent? not blowing up? that's all
📋 Information Hierarchy — Price Flows from Most Informed to Least
Hedge funds trade near the top of this chain. The current system weights the bottom heavily.
#SignalLead TimeCurrent WeightTarget Weight
1Options market (UOA, large sweeps)3–5 days ahead2 pts10+ pts
2Dark pool prints (>$1M off-exchange)1–3 days aheadMissingAdd
3Cluster insider buying (3+ execs, 30d)1–4 weeks ahead3 pts generic8–10 pts
4Post-earnings drift (PEAD, beat >10%)Ongoing, 21-day window+2 bonusPrimary Tier 1 catalyst
5Price / volume action (breakout, VCP)Real-timeWell weighted ✓Keep
6Analyst upgrades / downgradesLagging 1–2 weeks4 ptsReduce — often priced
7Fundamentals (ROE, D/E, PEG)Quarterly lag30 ptsCut to 15 pts quality gate only
8Reddit / Twitter sentimentUsually contrarianScoredContrarian signal only
✅ Catalyst Taxonomy — Every BUY Needs a Named Catalyst
"Good technicals" is not a catalyst. A catalyst is a specific event creating buying pressure right now.
TierCatalystWin RateDuration
TIER 1PEAD — EPS beat >10%, within 21 days, price holding gap63–68%3–21 days
TIER 152-week high breakout on volume ≥1.5× average61%3–10 days
TIER 1VCP (3+ contractions) + Pocket Pivot on same day65%+3–7 days
TIER 1UOA — large OTM call sweep 1–3 days ago58–62%3–7 days
TIER 2Sector ETF making new highs (stock in top-1 rotating sector)+10–15% base rate5–15 days
TIER 2TTM Squeeze firing + rising OBV (compression → expansion)Strong2–5 days
TIER 2Short squeeze structural setup (float >20%, above 50 EMA, catalyst)Asymmetric1–5 days violent
TIER 3Analyst upgrade with PT above current priceLow — often priced1–2 days fade
TIER 3Positive news headlineVery LowFades in 1–2 days
NOISEReddit/WSB mentions, congressional trades, Elliott Wave labelsWeak / contrarianUnreliable
📋 The Trade Thesis Template — What a BUY Signal Should Look Like
NVDA — TIER 1 BUY @ $152.50

CATALYST: PEAD (earnings beat +18% EPS, 12 days ago, still drifting)
SETUP:    VCP 3 contractions complete, breakout pivot at $151.80
CONFIRM:  UOA detected ($155 calls, 3,000 contracts, 2 days ago)
          Pocket pivot (today vol 2.1× max down-day vol in 10d)
          XLK (sector) outperforming SPY by +3.2% this week

ENTRY:    $151.80–$153.00 (within 1% of pivot)
STOP:     $148.20 (below 21 EMA, 1.2× ATR) — risk $3.30/share

🌞 4-Regime Market Playbook
The current system has a binary bull/bear flag. Professionals use 4 distinct environments requiring completely different behavior. Regime determines everything: which setups work, how large to size, whether to be in cash.

⚡ Conviction Tiers & Dynamic Position Sizing
A score of 75 and a score of 95 both output BUY with identical position size. This is the single biggest edge being left on the table. Professional traders size by conviction.
🎯 Conviction Tier System — Replace Binary BUY/WATCH/AVOID
TierCriteriaAllocationEntry Behavior
TIER 1 Score ≥ 88 + named Tier 1 catalyst + UOA or cluster insider confirmation Full position (8–10%) Enter aggressively — don't wait for pullback
TIER 2 Score 78–87 + named Tier 1 or 2 catalyst Half position (4–5%) Wait for pullback to entry zone before entering
TIER 3 Score 70–77, setup only, no clear Tier 1 catalyst Quarter position (2–2.5%) Entry strictly at or below trigger price — no chasing
WATCH Score 60–69, not ready yet No position Set price alert — promote to Tier 3 if trigger fires on volume
AVOID Score < 60 or failed gate No position Do not touch
📊 Dynamic Position Sizing — Kelly Criterion
Current system: fixed 5–10% per position regardless of conviction, regime, or volatility. The right way:
Step-by-Step Formula
# Step 1: Base Kelly from tracker stats
kelly = (win% × avg_win/avg_loss - loss%) / (avg_win/avg_loss)
half_kelly = kelly × 0.5 # always use half

# Step 2: Conviction multiplier
tier_mult = {1: 1.0, 2: 0.6, 3: 0.3}

# Step 3: Regime multiplier
regime_mult = {bull: 1.0, neutral: 0.7, bear: 0.0}

# Step 4: VIX multiplier
vix_mult = max(0, 1 - (vix - 15) / 50)

# Step 5: Final allocation & shares
alloc = half_kelly × tier_mult × regime_mult × vix_mult
shares = (portfolio × alloc) / (entry - stop)
VIX Size Multiplier
VIXMultiplierMax New Size
< 151.0×Full allocation
15–200.9×90% of normal
20–250.7×70% of normal
25–300.5×Half size
> 300.0×No new longs

📊 Float Rotation — Institutional Accumulation Detector
Float Rotation = 5-day volume ÷ (shares outstanding × free float %)
A ratio above 1.0 means the entire float has changed hands — institutions are actively repositioning. This is one of the cleanest leading indicators of sustained price movement. Currently missing entirely.
< 0.5×
Low interest — institutions not active
0.5–1.0×
Normal — moderate institutional activity
> 1.0×
High conviction — entire float turned over
🚨 Exit Rules — Where Edge Is Made or Lost
Entry quality determines if you're in a good position. Exit quality determines if you make money. Most trading alpha is lost on exits, not entries. These 6 rules are systematic — no discretion needed.
1
Hard Stop — Immediate, No Debate
Price closes below the pre-defined stop level → sell everything at market open next day. No exceptions. No averaging down. No "it'll recover." The stop was the plan — honor it.
Current state: Stop exists in trade plan. No enforcement mechanism.
2
Time Stop — Day 5 Forced Exit
If price has not reached T1 by close of Day 5 → exit everything regardless of P&L. The thesis was for a 5-day move. If it hasn't moved, the thesis is wrong. Waiting longer converts a swing trade into a hope trade.
Current state: Completely missing. Picks stay open indefinitely.
3
T1 Partial Exit — Mandatory, Not Optional
When price reaches T1 (first target at 2:1) → sell exactly 50% of position, move stop to breakeven on remaining 50%. You now have a free trade. The remaining 50% rides to T2 with zero risk.
Current state: T1 flag exists in portfolio but no partial exit logic or tracking.
4
Trend Break — Same-Day Exit
For a momentum / breakout trade: price closes below 8 EMA after having been above it → exit same day at close. The momentum that justified the trade is gone. Don't wait for the hard stop — act on the signal.
Current state: Not implemented. EMA values are displayed but never used as exit triggers.
5
Volume Dry-Up — Institutional Exit Signal
On Day 3 or later: volume drops below 60% of 20-day average AND price stalls (less than 0.5% move) → exit. Institutions have stopped buying. The crowd is no longer interested. The move is over.
Current state: Not implemented.
6
Reversal Candle at Resistance — Immediate Exit
Bearish engulfing, shooting star, or strong red candle at a major S/R level → exit next morning at open. The rejection is information. The market is rejecting your thesis in real-time.
Current state: Candle patterns are detected and displayed. Never used as exit signal.
🚫 Losing Streak Protocol — When to Stop Trading
What does the system do when it has 3+ consecutive losses? Currently: nothing. Professional answer:
ConditionActionWhy
0–2 consecutive lossesContinue at full sizeNormal variance — expected in any system
3 consecutive lossesReduce all sizes by 50%System may be in unfavorable environment
5 consecutive lossesStop trading — reviewClear pattern — not variance, likely regime shift
Monthly P&L ≤ −5%No new positions rest of monthMonthly drawdown limit — capital preservation
💡 After any trading pause: review the last N losses. Are they the same setup type? Same regime? Same time of day? Pattern in losses = the system has a bug, not bad luck.

🎯 14 Live Scanners
Each scanner runs daily. Stocks that pass appear on the Strategies tab with full analysis.
#1 Core Swing Engine Breakout/Continuation WR 55-60% Hold 5-15d
5-pillar scoring on S&P 500 + Russell 1000. The main engine that scores every stock across technicals, catalysts, RS, smart money, and fundamentals.
#2 10-Week Pullback Trend Continuation WR 58-62% Hold 7-21d
Strong stocks pulling back to rising 50 SMA with RS >= 70. Classic institutional re-entry point. Best in Risk-On Trending regime.
#3 Mean Reversion Mean Reversion WR 50-55% Hold 3-7d
RSI < 30 bounce on stocks trading above their 200 SMA. Catches oversold snaps in fundamentally sound names. Tight stops, quick exits.
#4 Sector Rotation Breakout Expansion WR 52-56% Hold 7-14d
Identifies sector ETF breakouts and rides the leaders within rotating sectors. Follows institutional capital flows between sectors.
#5 VCP Breakout Breakout Expansion WR 55-60% Hold 7-21d
Volatility Contraction Pattern with 2+ contractions. Declining volume into the pivot, then expansion on breakout. Classic Minervini setup.
#6 Pocket Pivot Impulse Catalyst WR 53-57% Hold 5-10d
Volume exceeds the maximum down-day volume in the prior 10 bars. Gil Morales signal indicating institutional accumulation without a breakout.
#7 RS New High Trend Continuation WR 56-60% Hold 7-21d
Relative Strength >= 90 and price near 52-week high. The strongest stocks in the market, likely to continue outperforming.
#8 Insider Buying Special Situation WR 54-58% Hold 10-30d
2+ insider purchases within 30 days. Open-market buys by officers/directors signal high confidence. Longer hold for the thesis to play out.
#9 Gap Holds Impulse Catalyst WR 52-56% Hold 3-7d
3%+ gap up that holds above the gap level through the session. Institutional demand absorbing all selling. Trade the continuation.
#10 Short Squeeze Special Situation WR 45-52% Hold 3-10d
Short float > 10% with price trending up. Forced covering creates rapid upside. Higher risk, binary outcome. Use tight stops.
#11 Earnings Run-Up Impulse Catalyst WR 55-60% Hold 7-14d
7-14 days before earnings with 75%+ historical beat rate. Institutional front-running of expected positive results. Exit before the report.
#12 Golden Cross Trend Continuation WR 52-56% Hold 14-30d
50 SMA crossing above 200 SMA. Long-term trend reversal signal. Slower setup with longer hold period. Best for patient swing positions.
#13 Bull Flag Breakout Expansion WR 54-58% Hold 5-14d
Impulse move followed by tight consolidation with declining volume. The flag pattern resolves with a volume expansion breakout.
#14 Volume Breakout Breakout Expansion WR 53-57% Hold 5-14d
Price breaks above 20-day high on 2x+ average volume. Raw institutional demand signal. Simple but effective when filtered by RS and regime.

• Per Trade % = maximum allocation of total equity to a single position

• All profiles use the same scoring engine — only sizing and strategy access differ
✅ Trading Rules
Non-negotiable risk management rules. Breaking any one of these rules is the fastest path to account destruction. Discipline is the edge.
⚠
Rule 1: Max 1 position per sector
Concentration in one sector = correlation risk. 3 tech stocks act like 1 position during a sector sell-off. Diversify across sectors.
🔐
Rule 2: Always set stop-loss before entry
No trade without a defined stop. Calculate your stop (1.25x ATR below support) BEFORE clicking buy. Enter the stop order immediately after entry fills.
🚫
Rule 3: Never move a stop lower
Moving your stop down turns a small planned loss into a large unplanned one. This is the #1 account killer for retail traders. The stop is sacred.
🎯
Rule 4: Exit at T1 (50%), trail remainder
When price hits Target 1, sell half the position and move the stop to breakeven. The remaining 50% rides with a trailing stop on EMA21. This locks in profit.
⏰
Rule 5: Max hold period per setup family
Impulse Catalyst: 5-8 days. Breakout Expansion: 7-21 days. Trend Continuation: 7-21 days. Special Situation: 5-15 days. Exit at day-max regardless if T1 has not been hit.
🛑
Rule 6: No trading in Panic regime (VIX > 35)
When VIX exceeds 35, institutional liquidation cascades are in progress. Longs bought during panic historically lose before recovering. Cash is a position.
⚡
Rule 7: 3 consecutive losses = pause 2 days
Three losses in a row signals either the regime shifted or your execution is off. Pause for 2 trading days. Review the trades. Resume at half size.
📈
Rule 8: Down 10% from peak = cut size to 50%
If account equity drops 10% from its peak, reduce all new position sizes to 50% of normal. Capital preservation mode. Focus on A+ setups only until equity recovers.
📊 Technical Matrix Indicators
Every indicator shown in the Technical Matrix explained — what each signal means and how it contributes to the overall score.
📈EMAs (5/8/13/20/50/200)
EMA 5/8
Ultra-short-term momentum. Used for scalp entries and trailing stops on impulse trades.
EMA 13
Short-term trend filter. Price above 13 = bullish short-term bias.
EMA 20/21
The workhorse. Primary trend line for swing trades. Pullbacks to EMA21 in uptrend = entry.
EMA 50
Medium-term trend. Institutional reference line. 10-week moving average equivalent.
EMA 200
Long-term trend. Bull/bear market divider. Price above 200 = bull market for that stock.
📊MACD (12/26/9)
Signal Line Cross
MACD crossing above signal line = bullish. Below = bearish. Primary momentum trigger.
Histogram Direction
Rising histogram = accelerating momentum. Declining = decelerating.
Zero Line Cross
MACD crossing above zero = medium-term trend shift bullish. Strong confirmation signal.
💰VWAP
Institutional Fair Value
Volume-Weighted Average Price. Where institutions see fair value for the session.
Above VWAP
Buyers in control. Institutional demand exceeding supply. Bullish intraday.
Below VWAP
Sellers in control. Institutional supply exceeding demand. Wait for reclaim.
📈Volume / RVOL
RVOL (Relative Volume)
Today volume vs 20-day average. 1.5x+ = institutional. 2x+ = heavy accumulation.
Volume Trend
Rising vol on up days + declining vol on down days = accumulation.
OBV (On-Balance Volume)
Cumulative volume flow. Rising OBV with flat price = stealth accumulation.
📋EMA Stack
Full Bull (8>13>20>50)
All short EMAs stacked above longer EMAs in order. Strongest trend alignment. Max score.
Partial Bull
Some EMAs aligned but not all. Trend is developing or weakening. Partial score.
Bearish Stack
Short EMAs below long EMAs. Downtrend. Zero trend score. Only valid for shorts.
🔥RSI (14-period Wilder)
Overbought (>70)
Stock is extended. Not an automatic sell, but new entries carry risk.
Bullish Zone (50-70)
Healthy momentum. Sweet spot for swing entries. RSI 55-65 with rising trend = ideal.
Oversold (<30)
Extreme selling. Mean reversion opportunity IF stock is above 200 SMA.
Divergence
Price making new highs while RSI makes lower highs = bearish divergence.
☁Ichimoku Cloud
Cloud as S/R
The Kumo acts as a dynamic support/resistance zone. Thicker cloud = stronger S/R.
TK Cross
Tenkan-sen (9) crossing Kijun-sen (26). Bullish cross above cloud = strong buy signal.
Price vs Cloud
Price above cloud = bullish trend. Inside cloud = consolidation. Below = bearish.
💪ADX (Trend Strength)
ADX > 25
Strong trend present. Trade with the trend. Breakout and continuation setups work best.
ADX 15-25
Developing or weakening trend. Be cautious. Mean reversion may work.
ADX < 15
No trend. Range-bound. Avoid breakout strategies. Wait for ADX to rise.
+DI / -DI Cross
+DI above -DI = bullish trend shift. Below = bearish. Combine with ADX > 25.

Gate: Each pillar scored independently; normalization: tech_norm = tech/38×30, total/90×100
  • Optionality (20): R:R ratio + UOA (5pts) + PEAD (4pts) + catalyst quality
  • Fundamentals (30): Revenue growth, margins, EPS beat rate, Zacks rank, PEG
  • Technicals (30, extended to 38): EMA stack, RVOL, RSI (Wilder), MACD, VCP, ADX
  • Sentiment (10): News bias, StockTwits, insider buys, short interest, congressional
  • Bonuses: Elliott Wave ±3, TV Rating ±3, Gmail Zacks ±5, weekly EMA ±2

Gate: All gates must clear for T1; each lower tier relaxes one gate

Gate: EXTENDED or MISSED blocks T1 assignment; FRESH adds size confidence

  • PULLBACK: Within 4% of EMA50 — continuation pullback to confluence

IN: Historical win rate/avg win/avg loss, regime, VIX, conviction tier, portfolio size
OUT: Allocation % + suggested shares
▶ Half-Kelly × Regime Mult × VIX Mult × Conviction Tier Mult → $ risk → shares
Gate: Capped at 15% per position regardless of Kelly output
  • Kelly fraction = (W×P − L×(1−P)) / W where P=win_rate, W=avg_win, L=avg_loss
  • Half-Kelly = Kelly / 2 (risk of ruin protection)
  • Regime mult: Bull=1.0 / Neutral=0.75 / Bear=0.5
  • VIX mult: <20→1.0 / 20–25→0.75 / 25–30→0.5 / >30→0.25
  • Tier mult: T1=1.0 / T2=0.5 / T3=0.25

  • Losing streak protocol: 3 losses → half size; 5 losses → pause review

OUT: 6 explicit exit rules per position
▶ compute_trade_plan() exit_rules block — rule cascade stored with each position
Gate: Rules evaluated at portfolio server refresh; alerts sent via Mac notification + Slack
  • Rule 1 — Hard Stop: Exit ALL at stop price immediately — no averaging, no exceptions
  • Rule 2 — Time Stop: Exit ALL by Day 5 if flat (<+1% from entry) — kills dead trades
  • Rule 3 — T1 Partial: Sell 50% at T1, move stop to breakeven on remainder
  • Rule 4 — Trend Break: Exit ALL on daily close below 8 EMA
  • Rule 5 — Volume Dry-Up: Exit on 3 consecutive below-avg-vol days during rally
  • Rule 6 — Reversal Candle: Exit at open on shooting star / bearish engulfing at resistance
↓
📈
STAGE 10 PERFORMANCE ATTRIBUTION ● ROADMAP
IN: Closed trades from tracker.json with catalyst_tags, regime, entry_quality, setup_type
OUT: Win rate × profit factor sliced by 4 dimensions
▶ compute_stats() + future compute_attribution() — tells you WHERE the edge is
Gate: Requires ≥5 closed trades; attribution by: catalyst / regime / setup / entry quality
  • Win rate by catalyst: PEAD vs UOA vs VCP vs SQUEEZE vs BREAKOUT
  • Win rate by regime: Risk-On Trending vs Choppy vs Risk-Off
  • Win rate by setup: Stage 2 vs Pullback vs SAR Reversal vs Squeeze Breakout
  • Win rate by entry quality: FRESH vs VALID vs EXTENDED
  • Profit factor by time-in-trade: Day 1–5 exit vs Day 5+ (time stop efficiency)
  • Goal: deprecate setups with PF <1.2 and promote setups with PF >2.0

Regime BUY Bar Min R:R Max Size Allowed Setups

🪙 Crypto Assessment — How It Works
A rules-based, regime-aware screener that finds the best 10–15 swing setups from the top 100 coins by market cap. Combines CoinGecko universe data, Binance real-time pricing, futures funding rates, 4h MACD/EMA technical analysis, DexScreener on-chain liquidity, and the Fear & Greed Index. Buy/sell decisions require 4h MACD confirmation.
1
Universe — CoinGecko Top 100
Start from the top 100 coins ranked by market cap via CoinGecko's /coins/markets endpoint. This gives real market-cap ranking, not self-reported data. Fields collected per coin: current price, market cap, 24h/7d/30d price change, ATH, 24h high/low, and image.
2
Hard Eliminators — 6 gates applied in order
1 Stablecoin — symbol in USDT, USDC, DAI, BUSD, FRAX, etc. Eliminated immediately.
2 Wrapped / Synthetic — WBTC, stETH, wstETH, cbBTC, etc. Not native assets, skip.
3 Market cap < $1B — Below this threshold, liquidity and price discovery are unreliable.
4 24h volume < $50M — Can't move size into a position with less than $50M daily flow.
5 Vol/Market Cap < 1.5% — Catches large-cap zombies that exist but nobody trades.
6 BTC crash regime — If BTC is down >10% in 7 days, all alts are force-set to AVOID.
3
BTC Market Regime — assessed first, gates everything
The regime determines whether to trade at all and how aggressively:

BULL BTC 7d >+5% AND 30d >+10% → Full scan. If BTC dominance also falling, alt season active.
NEUTRAL Everything else → Normal scan. Apply all gates normally.
BEAR BTC 7d <-10% OR 30d <-20% → No new alts. Only BTC/ETH setups considered.

Also check Fear & Greed: Extreme Fear (<25) = capitulation zone, potential reversal. Extreme Greed (>75) = reduce size, don't chase breakouts.
4
Scoring — 100 points across 4 pillars
Momentum   25 pts
24h in -3% to +3%: +10 (not extended)
24h +3% to +8%: +5 (trending)
7d positive: +5
30d >+5%: +5
RSI proxy (7d <18%): +5
Volume   20 pts
RVOL >1.5x: +10
RVOL 1.0–1.5x: +7
RVOL <0.6x: 0
Rising vol trend: +10
Structure   20 pts
ATH -10% to -30%: +10 (base)
ATH -30% to -50%: +7
Day range <5%: +6
Price top 25% of range: +4
Technical (4h)   35 pts
MACD (12,26,9) — 20 pts:
Golden cross: +20
Bullish momentum (above zero): +15
Bullish (below zero): +8
Death cross: 0

EMA Stack (5,8,13,20,50) — 15 pts:
Bullish stack (P>5>8>13>20>50): +15
4+ EMAs below price: +10
3 EMAs below: +7
Bearish stack: 0
EMA 5/13 golden cross bonus: +3
5
Funding Rate Overlay — ±5 points
Binance futures funding rate tells you how leveraged the market is:

Healthy -0.01% to +0.01% → +5 pts. Market not crowded, clean setup.
Mild Outside healthy band but not extreme → +2 pts.
Crowded Short Rate < -0.02% → +3 pts. Squeeze candidate — shorts will be forced out.
Crowded Long Rate > +0.05% → -5 pts. Longs are too crowded, fade signal.

Only available for coins with Binance perpetual futures. Coins without perps use base score only.
5b
Williams Fractals Overlay — ±3 points
5-bar Williams Fractals on 4h candles identify dynamic support and resistance:

Up Fractal Swing high — bar with the highest high surrounded by 2 lower highs on each side. Marks resistance.
Down Fractal Swing low — bar with the lowest low surrounded by 2 higher lows on each side. Marks support.

Scoring:
BREAKOUT Price above last resistance fractal → +3 pts. Confirmed breakout.
SUPPORT TEST Price within 2% of last support fractal → +2 pts. Bounce setup.
BREAKDOWN Price below last support fractal → -3 pts. Support lost.
BETWEEN S/R Price between fractal levels → 0 pts. Neutral zone.

Fractal levels are shown as R: (resistance) and S: (support) on cards and in the table.
6
Decision Thresholds — MACD-confirmed
BUY Score ≥ 70 AND 4h MACD bullish/golden cross — both score and technicals must confirm.
WATCH Score ≥ 70 but MACD not confirming, OR score 50–69 — wait for alignment.
AVOID Score < 50 — structure or momentum not there yet.

Override rules:
● 4h MACD death cross forces any BUY → WATCH (never enter against a fresh death cross).
● BTC regime BEAR → all alts forced to AVOID. Only BTC/ETH retain scored decisions.
7
Grouping — by token category
Core Major Bitcoin, Ethereum — always evaluated regardless of regime.
L1 Platform Native layer-1 blockchains with market cap >$5B (SOL, ADA, AVAX, TON…).
Infrastructure / DeFi Exchange tokens, oracles, DeFi protocols (BNB, LINK, UNI, AAVE…).
Speculative Large Cap Everything else that passes the gates — narrative and momentum plays.
8
Real-Time Pricing — Binance WebSocket
Top Picks card prices update live via Binance's public mini-ticker WebSocket stream (wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/!miniTicker@arr). No API key required. The connection opens when you navigate to the Crypto tab and closes when you leave. Score, decision, and pillar data are from the scan run time — only the price field refreshes live.

📚 SwingTrade Playbook
What the system does, when it runs, how to read the dashboard, and how to stop it.
🎯 What the system is
A rule-based swing trading engine running on your Mac. It scans ~1,000 US stocks hourly during market hours, scores them on 5 pillars (Tech, Catalyst, RS, Smart Money, Quality), and ranks BUY / WATCH / SHORT / AVOID with explicit entry zones, stop, and target prices.
Execution: Alpaca paper account ($100K test equity, capped to $5K gross via config). Bracket orders (entry limit + stop-loss + take-profit) submitted automatically. No manual execution — the system trades mechanically so discretion can't leak edge.
Goal: 60-day paper track record proving live WR ≥ 65% before real money.
⏰ A day in the life (all times Pacific)
1:00–5:00am
Pre-market scans. Scheduler runs swing_trade.py hourly. Fetches Polygon OHLCV, FMP fundamentals, Finviz, Zacks email. Each run produces cache/last_bundle.json + regenerates the dashboard. You can ignore these or glance at the System Status tab if curious.
6:30am
US market opens (9:30am ET). Nothing automated — orders not yet live.
6:35am
⚡ Executor fires. Reads last_bundle.json → submits paper bracket orders for every BUY signal via Alpaca. Limit entry + OCO stop/target in one atomic order. You get a Mac notification on each submission. Log: cache/logs/executor_YYYY-MM-DD.log.
6:40am–12:50pm
Fill monitor runs every 10 min. Cancels any limit order unfilled after 10 minutes (prevents dead limits lingering through the day). Also runs hourly scans.
12:55pm
🕑 EOD manager fires. Reads open positions, applies exit rules: stop-hit, target-hit, max-hold day limit, gap-down insurance, runner-trim (if any position > 25% of equity), flat-position release. Submits market SELL for exits; cancels+resubmits stops for tightens. 5 min before market close.
1:00pm
Market closes (4:00pm ET). No more orders accepted.
2:00–5:00pm
Post-close scans. Capture end-of-day data for next morning's signals.
Sat 2:00am
Weekly backtest. Full 252-day portfolio simulation with current code. Updates config._meta.last_backtested so the dashboard footer shows "Backtested 2026-04-18 · WR 78.3%" (or whatever the fresh number is).
📄 Where to look in the dashboard
QuestionTab / Section
"What's on the radar today?"Trades tab — BUY / WATCH / SHORT sections, ranked by score. Tile colors: green accent = BUY, yellow = WATCH, red = SHORT.
"Am I actually making money?"Portfolio tab — Equity, Cash, Today's P&L, MTD, Gross Exposure, Risk pill, open positions, closed trades.
"Which setups are working?"Performance tab + python3 leaderboard.py — per-setup WR, PF, expectancy, size recommendation.
"Is there a data or config problem?"System Status → Config Integrity (threshold conflicts) + Data Health (null %, failover, kill rate).
"How far through paper trading am I?"System Status → Validation (P7) — Day N/60 progress bar, go-live gates.
"Is live drifting from backtest?"System Status → Drift Monitor + python3 drift_check.py --slack.
"Why didn't X fire?"cache/logs/scan_YYYY-MM-DD.log — auto-logs top 10 high-RS tickers + their blocking reason.
"What's still on the roadmap?"System Status → Roadmap (reads OPEN_ITEMS.md live).
🛡 What to do when you see...
0 BUYs for days in a row
✓ Normal. Choppy regime (risk_on_choppy) raises buy_min to 72. In bull quiet tape, top scores often sit at 68–70. Do not lower thresholds manually. The system is protecting you from marginal setups. Wait for volatility or sector rotation.
Live WR drifting >15 pts below backtest
⚠ Investigate. Drift alerter will flag in System Status → Drift Monitor. Most common causes: (1) regime mismatch — backtest window was bullier than live; (2) survivorship bias in the backtest universe; (3) real-world slippage vs. 3bps model. Don't tune thresholds yet — need ≥ 30 live trades before any adjustment.
A position gaps down > 3% at open
✓ Auto-handled. AI-46 gap-down insurance in EOD manager auto-submits market SELL. Log entry: Gap down -X.Y% at open — binary bad news.
Portfolio down -4% in a day
✓ Auto-handled. AI-45 daily-loss halt blocks all new BUYs that scan. Open positions continue per their normal exit rules.
VIX spikes +30% in a day
✓ Auto-handled. AI-11 VIX kill switch blocks new longs, reduces size to 0.2×. All pending BUYs demoted to WATCH for that scan.
Bad regime transition (risk-on → risk-off)
⚠ Partially auto. Regime-transition alert fires (Mac notification). Auto-exit trims positions > 10% of equity down to 5%. Banner appears in dashboard top strip.
PDT counter hits 3/5d
✓ Auto-blocked. All new BUYs demoted to WATCH until counter decays. Prevents the SEC 4-trade rule from triggering on sub-$25K accounts.
🚫 Kill switches
Soft stop (keep positions, stop new trades)
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.swingtrade.executor.plist
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.swingtrade.eod.plist
Open positions continue running with their Alpaca-side stop-loss orders intact. Nothing new enters.
Hard stop (close everything NOW)
/Volumes/MyMacDisk/Claude\ Skills/SwingTrade/emergency_close_all.sh
5-second Ctrl-C window, then cancels all open orders + market-sells all open positions. Use only if something has clearly gone sideways.
Restart everything
for p in executor eod fill daily weekly-backtest; do
  launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.swingtrade.$p.plist
  launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.swingtrade.$p.plist
done
📈 Day-60 go-live gate
After 60 calendar days of paper trading, the system grades itself automatically (System Status → Validation). Real-money deployment requires all 6 gates green:
✓ Live WR ≥ 65%
✓ Max drawdown ≤ 12%
✓ executor.py ran cleanly for 5+ consecutive days
✓ eod_manager.py present and firing
✓ Alpaca keys valid in .env
✓ Setup distribution matches backtest
If any fail at day-60, add 30 days and re-evaluate. Don't rationalize a partial pass.
🔒 Safety guarantees
✓ Paper only. Executor + EOD manager are hardcoded to paper=True. Would fail fast if someone tried to flip it.
✓ Bracket orders. Every BUY submits entry + stop + target atomically. Stop is on Alpaca's servers, not mental.
✓ Hard daily halt. -4% portfolio P&L blocks new longs.
✓ Drawdown kill. -8% open P&L blocks all new entries.
✓ 3-consecutive-loss circuit breaker. Pauses entries after 3 losses.
✓ PDT rule. Blocks at 3/5d day-trades if equity < $25K.
✓ No secrets in git. All API keys + webhooks in .env (git-ignored).

💡 Rules of engagement (for you)
✗ Don't override BUY decisions. If the system says no, trust the system.
✗ Don't widen stops. Ever. The stop is the thesis.
✗ Don't kill switch during a drawdown. Drawdowns are normal; discretion kills edge.
✗ Don't retune thresholds before 30 live trades. Small samples lie.
✓ Do log observations. "Scan felt late on MSFT" — but don't act on it until you have 30 counterexamples.
✓ Do check Drift Monitor weekly. That's your early-warning system.
✓ Do run the weekly review. python3 weekly_review.py every Friday afternoon.
📖 Field Guide
Every badge, score, and label explained — hover badges on signal cards for quick tooltips.
💡Quick tip: Hover over any badge on a signal card (BUY, T2, Cat T1, EXTENDED, Trend Continuation…) to see a one-line tooltip explaining that field. This guide has the full detail behind each concept.
🎯Verdict — BUY / WATCH / SHORT
BUY BUY
All thresholds met for the current regime: score ≥ regime min, R:R ≥ 3:1 (4:1 in Risk-Off), RS ≥ regime min, entry quality not MISSED, no gate failures. Act within the entry zone.
WATCH WATCH
Below one or more BUY thresholds — usually score, RS rank, or entry quality. Set a price alert at the entry zone and revisit when conditions improve. Not tradeable yet.
AVOID / SHORT SHORT
For longs: failed a hard gate (earnings blackout, liquidity, panic regime, MISSED entry). For shorts: bear score threshold met in a bearish regime.
📊Score /100 — 5 Pillars
Score /100 — 5-Pillar System
The composite score is built from five weighted pillars. Each pillar is scored independently and normalized to its weight. A score of 80+ is strong; 70–79 is solid; below 65 is marginal.
⚙️ Tech Structure (35 pts)
EMA stack (8/21/50/200), ADX trend strength, RSI/MACD momentum, RVOL, OBV, S/R structure, RS rank vs SPY, weekly EMA alignment, ADX+DI cross, VWAP, candle patterns.
⚡ Catalyst Quality (20 pts)
What is actually driving the move. Scores the type and strength of the catalyst — earnings surprise, options flow, breakout, squeeze, or pure momentum. Catalyst T1 contributes more than T3.
📊 RS + Sector (20 pts)
Relative strength of the stock vs SPY (RS Rank 0–100), plus whether the stock's sector is rotating into favour vs SPY over 63 days. Sector outperformance adds a 10% bonus.
🏦 Smart Money (15 pts)
Unusual options activity (UOA), institutional holding trends, insider buy/sell activity, short interest, and days-to-cover (squeeze risk).
🛡️ Quality Gate (10 pts)
Fundamental health: revenue growth, margin quality, EPS growth trend, balance sheet, PEG ratio, analyst consensus. Acts as a tiebreaker for otherwise equal setups.
🌐Market Regime
Risk-On Trending — BUY ≥ 65, R:R ≥ 3.0, RS ≥ 80
VIX < 18, breadth > 65% of stocks above 50d EMA, SPY above both EMAs. Full aggression. All setup families valid. Full position sizing (100%).
Risk-On Choppy — BUY ≥ 72, R:R ≥ 3.0, RS ≥ 75
Market is up but choppy — uncertain breadth or elevated VIX (18–25). Prefer pullbacks, PEAD, UOA, high-quality continuations. Size 70% of normal.
Risk-Off Trending — BUY ≥ 78, R:R ≥ 4.0, RS ≥ 80
SPY below 50d EMA or downtrending. Only elite leaders with exceptional catalysts. Max 35% of normal position size. Defensive sectors preferred.
PANIC — No new longs
VIX > 35 or fewer than 20% of stocks above their 50d EMA. Capital preservation mode. Existing positions managed to exits only.
📍Entry Quality (ATR-relative)
FRESH
Optimal. Price is within 0.75 ATR of the support level or EMA21. You are entering right at the logical support — stop is tight, R:R is maximised. Enter now.
PULLBACK
Good. Price has pulled back within 1.25 ATR of EMA8, EMA21, EMA50, or a key support level. Slightly less optimal than FRESH but still a quality entry. Risk is well-defined.
VALID
Acceptable. Within 1.25 ATR of a pivot. Not ideal but within risk tolerances. Consider waiting for a shallower pullback if you have time.
EXTENDED
Caution. Price is 1.25–2.0 ATR above the pivot or EMA21. You are chasing a move. The system requires an extra 10 score points to approve a BUY here. Waiting for a pullback will nearly always produce a better trade.
MISSED
Do not enter. Price is more than 2.0 ATR above the pivot. Entering here destroys the R:R ratio. Wait for a pullback to the next support or EMA, then re-evaluate as a FRESH or PULLBACK entry.
🏆Conviction Tiers — T1 / T2 / T3
T1
Highest conviction. ALL of: score ≥ 88, RS ≥ 85, R:R ≥ 3.5, regime = Risk-On Trending, catalyst tier = T1, entry quality = FRESH or PULLBACK. Use 8–10% allocation. Rare — expect 1–3 per month in a good regime.
T2
Standard quality trade. Score ≥ 78, RS ≥ 75, R:R ≥ 3.0, regime ≠ Panic, catalyst tier ≤ T2, quality entry. Use 5–7.5% allocation. Core of the trading book — target 2–4 concurrent T2 positions.
T3
Lower conviction. Score ≥ 70, R:R ≥ 3.0. One or more quality criteria missed (RS, regime, catalyst). Use 3–5% allocation. Treat as a speculative small position, not a core trade.
⚡Catalyst Tiers — Cat T1 / T2 / T3
Cat T1
Highest urgency. PEAD (Post-Earnings Announcement Drift — stock gapping up on earnings surprise), UOA (Unusual Options Activity — smart money positioning before a move), VCP breakout (Volatility Contraction Pattern), 52-week high breakout. These are time-sensitive: the window closes in days.
Cat T2
Mid-strength. Squeeze expansion, EMA21/50 pullback, institutional flow (increasing holdings), insider cluster (multiple buys in 30 days). Good setups but require technical confirmation before entry.
Cat T3
Weakest. Analyst price target upgrade, general momentum continuation, social sentiment spike. The thesis rests mainly on technicals, not a specific event. Still tradeable but use tighter size and expect slower moves.
🔍Entry Subtypes
Pivot Entry
First entry right at the breakout pivot or support level. Lowest risk. Best R:R. This is the ideal entry for any setup.
First Pullback
First pullback after the initial breakout. Classic stage-2 add point. Slightly higher entry than Pivot but confirmed breakout reduces false-break risk.
EMA21 Continuation
Price pulled back to the rising 21-day EMA during an uptrend. One of the most reliable trend-following entries. Stop goes just below EMA21.
EMA50 Continuation
Deeper pullback to the 50-day EMA. Requires strong underlying trend conviction. Better R:R than EMA21 entry but needs volume and sector confirmation.
Tight Range Rebreak
Stock compressed into a tight range (low ATR) and is breaking out again. Volatility contraction followed by expansion. Clean stop just below the range.
Breakout Add
Adding to an existing position after the initial breakout has already occurred and confirmed. Higher risk than a Pivot Entry. Only valid with positive open profit on the base position.
📅Setup Families & Hold Periods
Impulse Catalyst · Hold 5–8 days
Fast-moving, event-driven. Triggered by PEAD, unusual options, or gap-and-go on news. Trade the momentum window aggressively — take 50% profit at T1, trail the rest. Exit before day 8 regardless; impulse windows close fast.
Breakout Expansion · Hold 7–21 days
Classic stage-2 breakout from a VCP, squeeze, or 52-week high. Needs above-average volume on the breakout day. Ride the expansion phase; re-evaluate at 14 days if still open.
Trend Continuation · Hold 7–21 days
Stock in a confirmed uptrend pulling back to EMA21 or EMA50. The trend is your edge — enter on the bounce, hold as long as the EMA stack holds. Exit on a close below EMA21 after T1 is hit.
Special Situation · Hold 5–15 days
Non-standard catalyst: insider cluster, float rotation, short squeeze. Higher volatility and binary outcomes. Use tighter stops (1.0× ATR vs 1.5× for trend setups). Catalysts are often time-limited — have a defined exit plan before entering.
💰Position Sizing
Base Allocation
The Kelly formula calculates the theoretically optimal fraction of capital per trade based on your historical win rate and average profit/loss. Raw Kelly is scaled down to 25% for safety (fractional Kelly).
Regime Multiplier
Risk-On Trending = 1.0 (full size) · Risk-On Choppy = 0.70 · Risk-Off Trending = 0.35 · Panic = 0.0. If VIX is 22–25, an additional 0.75× VIX multiplier is applied on top.
Conviction Tier Multiplier
T1 = 0.85–1.0 (full size) · T2 = 0.30–0.60 · T3 = 0.15–0.30. Final position = base × regime_mult × vix_mult × tier_mult. Hard caps: max 10% per position, max 80% gross exposure.
Beta Adjustment (β shown on card)
Beta measures how much the stock moves vs the S&P 500. A stock with β 0.5 moves half as much — so you need 2× shares to match the dollar risk of a β 1.0 stock. β > 1.5 triggers a downward size adjustment (already volatile enough). The '→ X% size adj' label shows the final % adjustment applied.
R:R (Reward-to-Risk Ratio)
R:R = (T1 Price − Entry) ÷ (Entry − Stop). Minimum 3:1 required in Risk-On regimes. 4:1 required in Risk-Off. A 3:1 means you risk $1 to make $3. Even at a 40% win rate, 3:1 R:R is profitable.
📋Trade Plan Fields
Entry Zone (entry_lo – entry_hi)
The acceptable price range for entry. Calculated as a ±1% band around the current price adjusted for ATR. If the price gaps above entry_hi on open, downgrade to WATCH and wait.
Stop
The hard exit level. Calculated as 1.5× ATR below the nearest support. Close the position if price closes a full session below this level. Never widen the stop after entry — that is how small losses become large ones.
T1 — First Target
Take 50% of the position off at T1. Move the stop to breakeven. T1 is typically the next resistance level or 2× risk above entry.
T2 — Second Target
Hold the remaining 50% with a trailing stop at 1.5× ATR. T2 is a stretch target at the next major resistance or 3–4× risk above entry. Let this run — this is where the outsized returns come from.
Hold Period Guide
The expected duration from entry to T2, by setup family. Impulse Catalyst: 5–8d. Breakout Expansion: 7–21d. Trend Continuation: 7–21d. Special Situation: 5–15d. Exit at day-max regardless of profit/loss if T1 has not been hit.
